Definition: a leaf (as coming up on a tree); collectively, foliage
BiblicalUsage: The leaf of a tree, and the Bible uses it at both ends of the story. After the fall Adam and Eve sew fig leaves together and make themselves aprons, the first human cover-up. And the righteous man is a tree planted by the rivers of water whose leaf also shall not wither, green in every season because his roots are in the law of the LORD.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for a leaf carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the two trees, that the leaf sewn to hide shame withers and the leaf rooted by the water does not.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
